messages:
maya_support: FYI customer 'acme-data' reports promo credits were consumed BEFORE their free-tier credits. They got a $12.50 charge on invoice 2026-03-01-ACME-77. Dashboard still shows free-tier remaining. Need triage, ETA to customer, and mitigation. Account: acct_9Z7abcd. Root ts: 1763245599 (from customer).

billing-bot: :receipt: new support ticket created #34218 for acct_9Z7abcd (auto).

jp_billing: On it. Can you paste the exact timestamps the customer sent and any raw usage rows? Also which model / endpoint they hit?

maya_support: Customer included this snippet: "We queried usage for 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z-2026-03-02T00:00:00Z and saw promo credits drop to 0 while free_tier stayed at 10k tokens. Then we received invoice charge. Dashboard shows free-tier remaining after the charge." They hit /v1/generate (gpt-3.5-compatible) around 2026-03-01T14:22:34Z.

jp_billing: I pulled the ledger for acct_9Z7abcd. Two credit buckets present: promo_2025Q4 (created_at: 2026-02-28T09:00:00Z, expires_at: 2026-04-01T00:00:00Z) and free_tier_2026 (created_at: 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, expires_at: 2026-12-31T23:59:59Z). Our credit-apply query currently orders by bucket_key DESC which is incorrect. Logs (redacted):
```
SELECT id, bucket_key, amount_remaining, expires_at FROM credits WHERE account_id='acct_9Z7abcd' ORDER BY bucket_key DESC LIMIT 10;
-- rows:
-- promo_2025Q4 | 10000 | 2026-04-01
-- free_tier_2026 | 10000 | 2026-12-31
```

ammar_eng: That ordering would cause lexicographic ordering to prefer "promo_..." over "free_tier_...". I can reproduce locally: call usage_apply_credit with two buckets, promo consumed first even though it expires sooner (or policy says free-tier should be consumed first for free-tier-preservation). Repro steps:
```
# repro (local)
curl -X POST https://billing.internal.redwood/v1/apply_credits \
  -d '{"account_id":"acct_9Z7abcd","usage_tokens":12000}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST_KEY"
# check credits table
psql -c "select bucket_key, amount_remaining from credits where account_id='acct_9Z7abcd' order by bucket_key desc;"
```

lina_escalations: Customer asked for immediate reversal if we charged them incorrectly. We should do manual refund and fix code. Can billing reverse and notify? I'll take point on customer comms.

jp_billing: I issued a manual reversal and applied a corrective credit for $12.50. Invoice 2026-03-01-ACME-77 status set to ADJUSTED (adj id: 2026-03-01-ACME-77-ADJ). Notified finance. Also opened PR to change ordering to: ORDER BY expires_at ASC, priority DESC. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/billing/pull/487 (tests included).

ammar_eng: I'll pick up PR review and push a patch to staging. I'll add unit tests for multiple buckets with mixed keys so we don't regress. ETA ~6h for staging->prod pipeline.

maya_support: Thanks — I told the customer we reversed the charge and are deploying a fix; asked them to check dashboard in 24h and confirm. I also asked them to forward any web console HAR if they still see mismatched numbers. :eyes:

jp_billing: Follow-up: logging shows the apply_credit function used the wrong comparator. Patch changes comparator and adds a guard when bucket.expiry == NULL. Also added a one-off migration to reconcile any accounts with promo > free_tier that were used first in March 2026 window. Migration queued: MIGRATE-2026-03-credit-order.

ammar_eng: Deploy completed to prod at 1763247400 (approx). Ran reconciliation job against acct_9Z7abcd; confirmed final balances: promo -> 10000, free_tier -> 8800 (after applying 12000 usage, free_tier reduced first). No other anomalies in the scan batch (first pass).

lina_escalations: Customer confirmed refund receipt and dashboard updated. Closing if no further customer issues. I'll monitor for 48h.

maya_support: Marking ticket #34218 resolved, will keep thread open for 48h for any regression. :white_check_mark:
